::: {.piege packages="ggplot2"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))

variable <- "cyl"
p <- ggplot(mtcars, mapping = aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(rows = .data[[variable]])
```
:::

## Why

In `aes()`, `.data` is the pronoun that refers to the data table. But `facet_grid()` and `facet_wrap()` evaluate their arguments right away, when you write the plot, outside of any table: `.data` has nothing to refer to yet, hence the error. The message talks about a "data mask", a notion you should not need to know to write a plot.

The formula form, `facet_grid(.data[[variable]] ~ .)`, does not fail, but the variable loses its name there: {ggplot2} stores it as `<unknown>`, which shows up for instance with `labeller = label_both`.

## The fix

`vars()` delays evaluation, like `aes()`, until the data is available. The variable then keeps its name.

::: {.piege packages="ggplot2"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))

p <- ggplot(mtcars, mapping = aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(.data[[variable]]))
ggplot_build(p)$layout$layout[, c("PANEL", "cyl")]
```
:::
